title: Bitwise AND of Numbers Range
summary: Given integers left and right indicating the range [left, right], provide the result of the bitwise AND operation applied to all numbers within this range, including both endpoints.
statement: Given integers left and right indicating the range [left, right], provide the result of the bitwise AND operation applied to all numbers within this range, including both endpoints.
constraints: AND every integer in the inclusive interval, not only the two endpoints. Very wide intervals must not be enumerated.
target_time_complexity: O(31), bounded by integer bit width
hints: A bit survives only if it is one in every number across the interval.
The answer is the common high-bit prefix of the endpoints, with lower varying bits cleared.
While right exceeds left, clear right's lowest set bit using right &= right-1; return the remaining prefix.
A single-value interval must return that value unchanged; wide intervals still need at most 31 bit-clearing steps.
editorial: Crossing the boundary represented by the right endpoint's lowest set bit means that bit cannot survive the full interval AND. Repeatedly clearing such bits leaves the shared high-bit prefix. The independent oracle explicitly ANDs all integers in bounded small ranges. Large direct fixtures span billions of integers and have simple known prefixes, ensuring that the reference does not depend on interval width.

tests.explanation: Binary 101 AND 110 AND 111 is 100, so the answer is 4; just ANDing 5 and 7 would incorrectly give 5.
The interval includes zero, so the AND of all its values is zero.
